Approval for mining mineral sand
409. SHRI N.K. PREMA-
CHANDRAN: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether the State Government of
Kerala has recommended any application
of Kerala Rare Earths Minerals Ltd. seeking
approval for mining mineral sand in the
coastal area of Alappuzha district in Kerala
to the Central Government;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken thereon;
(c) whether any authentic study has been
conducted on the environmental impact of
mining of beach sand minerals in the coastal
area of Alappuzha; and
(d) if so, the details of the study report?

PMRY in Assam
407. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of AGRO
AND RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) the target set to generate employment
opportunities under the Pradhan Mantri
Rozgar Yojana in the State of Assam during
the last four years, year-wise; and
(b) the number of educated unemployed
youths who have been benefited thereby in
the State?
Exploration of mineral sand of
Chavara in Kerala
408. SHRI N. K. PREMA-
CHANDRAN: Will the  PRIME
MINISTER  be pleased to state:
(a) what is the latest position of the joint
venture proposal in the public sector for the
explorations of mineral sand of Chavara in
Kerala in participations with NMDC, IRE
and KSIDC;
(b) whether there is any proposal to
disinvest the shares of NMDC and IRE;
and

Irradiation technique for food
processing
410. DR. DASARI NARAYANA
RAO: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether irradiation technique is
useful and cheap for food processing;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government propose to set
up irradiation facilities in Southern States
particularly in Andhra Pradesh; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Waiting list of telephone connections in
Karnataka
411. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the total number of people in the
waiting list for telephone connections in
Karnataka as on June, 2003, district-wise;
and
(b) by when these people are likely to be
provided with telephone connections?
Telephone subscribers in Delhi
412. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
DR. ABRAR AHMED:
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether subscribers of mobile
telephones run by private companies in Delhi
are more than that of MTNL's landline
connections;
(b) whether subscribers are surrendering
landline telephones in a large number and
switching over to mobile phones because
of MTNLs' poor and costly services; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
C.A.G. report on telephone system in
rural areas
†413. SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH
'LALAN':
SHRI LAJPAT RAI:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Comptroller
and Auditor General of India has, in its recent
report, criticized Government for un-
satisfactory telephone system in the rural areas;
(b) if so, the facts in this regard;
(c) whether Government have taken any
action for redressal of objections raised in
the report; and
(d) if so, the details of the action taken
thereon?
Privacy laws
414. SHRI RAJU PARMAR: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
cell phone location-services raise privacy
concerns;
(b) if so, Government's reaction thereto;
(c) whether there are any specific privacy
laws in India through which phone data can
be obtained by people not entitled to access;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
